questions.stem: Glucose and fructose have the same molecular formula (C₆H₁₂O₆) but differ in structure. They are called:
questions.explanation: Isomers — compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements and hence different properties. Glucose has an aldehyde group; fructose a ketone group — they taste differently (fructose is sweeter) and have different functions. Allotropes — different physical forms of the same element (diamond vs graphite for carbon). Isotopes — atoms of the same element with different neutron counts.

questions.stem: The sugar found in milk is:
questions.explanation: Lactose — the disaccharide found in milk — breaks down by the enzyme lactase into glucose + galactose. 'Lactose intolerance' is a deficiency of lactase. Sucrose is table sugar (from sugarcane / beet); glucose + fructose. Fructose — fruit sugar (also in honey). Maltose — from grain germination (barley); glucose + glucose.

questions.explanation: Proteins are chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. 20 standard amino acids build almost all proteins; 9 are 'essential' (must come from food). Fatty acids build lipids; nucleotides build DNA/RNA; monosaccharides build carbohydrates. Protein shape follows from sequence — a folding error can cause diseases (prion diseases, Alzheimer's).

questions.stem: The chemical messenger that carries information from DNA out of the nucleus to the ribosomes is:
questions.explanation: mRNA (messenger RNA) is transcribed from DNA in the nucleus and carries the genetic code to the ribosome, where it is translated into protein. tRNA (transfer RNA) brings amino acids to the ribosome and matches them to mRNA codons. rRNA (ribosomal RNA) is the structural RNA of the ribosome itself. miRNA (microRNA) is a short RNA that regulates gene expression.

questions.stem: Starch is stored in plants chiefly as a reserve of:
questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide of glucose — the main energy store in plants. Grain seeds (rice, wheat), tubers (potato) and roots (cassava) store starch. Iodine turns blue-black on contact with starch — the classic test. Animals store glucose as glycogen in liver / muscles. Cellulose (another glucose polymer) gives structural support to plant cell walls.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a water-soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins — Vitamin C and the eight B-complex vitamins. Not stored in large amounts; excess excreted in urine; must be eaten regularly. Fat-soluble — A, D, E, K — stored in liver / adipose tissue; hypervitaminosis possible if over-supplemented. Vitamin C sources: amla, citrus, guava, chilli.

options.option_text: Esters of glycerol and fatty acids

questions.explanation: Fats and oils are triglycerides — triesters of glycerol and three fatty acids. 'Fats' are solid at room temperature (animal fats, tropical oils); 'oils' are liquid (most vegetable oils). Saturated fats have no C=C double bonds; unsaturated fats have one (mono-) or more (poly-). Trans fats are partial hydrogenation products, considered unhealthy.
